instructions: Read the user's text aloud exactly as written, word for word, adding nothing. You are a warm, curious, conversational documentary narrator, explaining an idea to a friend. Use a flowing pace of about 175 words per minute, clear but never theatrical. Questions are genuine questions. Keep the same warm, level Cedar voice throughout. Short natural breaths at commas; no long pauses. Pronounce LoRA as low-rah, and Lean as leen.

lines.text: Ask a leading language model to add two three-hundred-digit numbers, and it's usually right.
lines.spoken: Ask a leading language model to add two three-hundred-digit numbers, and it's usually right.

lines.text: Here, one digit is wrong, and the answer gives no warning.
lines.spoken: Here, one digit is wrong, and the answer gives no warning.

lines.text: Passing yesterday's tests doesn't guarantee tomorrow's answer.
lines.spoken: Passing yesterday's tests doesn't guarantee tomorrow's answer.

lines.text: What if we could check every step a small model could ever take?
lines.spoken: What if we could check every step a small model could ever take?

lines.text: This is Sketchpad: a model that reads pictures and text, with about eight hundred million learned numbers, or weights, running in your browser.
lines.spoken: This is Sketchpad: a model that reads pictures and text, with about eight hundred million learned numbers, or weights, running in your browser.

lines.text: Watch it multiply, divide, factor a polynomial, and open a sheet inside a chat reply.
lines.spoken: Watch it multiply, divide, factor a polynomial, and open a sheet inside a chat reply.

lines.text: None of this calls a calculator or a tool. Every digit is computed by the model itself.
lines.spoken: None of this calls a calculator or a tool. Every digit is computed by the model itself.
lines.source: B (Abstract; Sheet machine: the runtime moves the view, the model computes every output digit)

lines.text: How does it do that?
lines.spoken: How does it do that?

lines.text: Like school arithmetic, it works on a sheet, one column at a time.
lines.spoken: Like school arithmetic, it works on a sheet, one column at a time.

lines.text: Each step sees only three printed cells and an instruction, never the whole problem or earlier steps.
lines.spoken: Each step sees only three printed cells and an instruction, never the whole problem or earlier steps.

lines.text: From that tiny image come a digit, a carry for the next column, and the next step.
lines.spoken: From that tiny image come a digit, a carry for the next column, and the next step.

lines.text: Simple code writes those outputs and moves the window.
lines.spoken: Simple code writes those outputs and moves the window.

lines.text: We trained about ten million extra weights—a small add-on called LoRA—while keeping the original model fixed.
lines.spoken: We trained about ten million extra weights—a small add-on called LoRA—while keeping the original model fixed.

lines.text: Why show it so little?
lines.spoken: Why show it so little?

lines.text: Longer numbers need more steps, but no new kinds of window.
lines.spoken: Longer numbers need more steps, but no new kinds of window.

lines.text: There are only two thousand, four hundred and forty-six possible views, counting the instructions.
lines.spoken: There are only two thousand, four hundred and forty-six possible views, counting the instructions.

lines.text: We can check every one.
lines.spoken: We can check every one.

lines.text: But does getting every window right mean getting the whole calculation right?
lines.spoken: But does getting every window right mean getting the whole calculation right?

lines.text: Yes, provided the code presents the right views: a correct step sets up the next correct step.
lines.spoken: Yes, provided the code presents the right views: a correct step sets up the next correct step.

lines.text: Lean, a computer proof checker, checks our proof for every length.
lines.spoken: Lean, a computer proof checker, checks our proof for every length.

lines.text: Written reasoning that rereads earlier steps keeps creating new situations; we also proved that finite testing alone cannot certify all those histories.
lines.spoken: Written reasoning that rereads earlier steps keeps creating new situations; we also proved that finite testing alone cannot certify all those histories.

lines.text: There's a practical catch: computers round numbers, and different chips round differently.
lines.spoken: There's a practical catch: computers round numbers, and different chips round differently.

lines.text: If the right digit wins by a hair, rounding could change the winner.
lines.spoken: If the right digit wins by a hair, rounding could change the winner.

lines.text: So we measure its lead over the strongest wrong answer—the margin—and check every view in the browser on a laptop's graphics processor.
lines.spoken: So we measure its lead over the strongest wrong answer—the margin—and check every view in the browser on a laptop's graphics processor.

lines.text: The smallest lead was three point zero two. Rounding would have to move a score by more than half of that, one point five one, to flip a digit; running views together in batches moved scores by at most one point zero nine.
lines.spoken: The smallest lead was three point zero two. Rounding would have to move a score by more than half of that, one point five one, to flip a digit; running views together in batches moved scores by at most one point zero nine.

lines.text: That repeatable record of the checks and margins is the certificate.
lines.spoken: That repeatable record of the checks and margins is the certificate.

lines.text: And on whole problems?
lines.spoken: And on whole problems?

lines.text: On two hundred and twenty sums and products fixed in advance, Sketchpad answered all two hundred and twenty; the strongest of ten other models answered two hundred and seventeen.
lines.spoken: On two hundred and twenty sums and products fixed in advance, Sketchpad answered all two hundred and twenty; the strongest of ten other models answered two hundred and seventeen.

lines.text: Without its sheet and adapter, the same small model answered twenty-three.
lines.spoken: Without its sheet and adapter, the same small model answered twenty-three.
lines.source: G (Fig. 1c / numbers.md: Qwen3.5-0.8B, no thinking, 23 of 220)

lines.text: Those checked procedures can also work together.
lines.spoken: Those checked procedures can also work together.

lines.text: A short program factors this cubic—a polynomial whose highest power is three—with every computed number coming from the model.
lines.spoken: A short program factors this cubic—a polynomial whose highest power is three—with every computed number coming from the model.

lines.text: The ordinary code arranging the steps and moving the view remains outside the proof.
lines.spoken: The ordinary code arranging the steps and moving the view remains outside the proof.

lines.text: But people ask questions, not just calculations.
lines.spoken: But people ask questions, not just calculations.

lines.text: So we trained a chat version to reach for its sheet by itself.
lines.spoken: So we trained a chat version to reach for its sheet by itself.

lines.text: First, the original model coached it on replies it wrote itself; then we rewarded it whenever its sheet gave the right answer.
lines.spoken: First, the original model coached it on replies it wrote itself; then we rewarded it whenever its sheet gave the right answer.

lines.text: Because the skill is an add-on, a dial called the gate can switch it off: at zero, the original model returns, bit for bit.
lines.spoken: Because the skill is an add-on, a dial called the gate can switch it off: at zero, the original model returns, bit for bit.

lines.text: Chat keeps that dial on, and there's a cost: on fresh grade-school word problems, it scores five point eight percentage points below the original.
lines.spoken: Chat keeps that dial on, and there's a cost: on fresh grade-school word problems, it scores five point eight percentage points below the original.

lines.text: We can also ask where a multiplication digit takes shape inside the model.
lines.spoken: We can also ask where a multiplication digit takes shape inside the model.

lines.text: At different processing layers, we pushed its internal state toward another digit.
lines.spoken: At different processing layers, we pushed its internal state toward another digit.

lines.text: Through layer fifteen, no tested answer changed; just after layer twenty, all eighty tested multiplication answers changed.
lines.spoken: Through layer fifteen, no tested answer changed; just after layer twenty, all eighty tested multiplication answers changed.

lines.text: Now give it two long numbers and watch it work.
lines.spoken: Now give it two long numbers and watch it work.

lines.text: It rechecks its weakest windows on your graphics processor; the full check is available for a new device.
lines.spoken: It rechecks its weakest windows on your graphics processor; the full check is available for a new device.

lines.text: The paper, code and model are open.
lines.spoken: The paper, code and model are open.
